label: Foundational case: actual, simple, unreceived, first, uncaused, incorruptible, under no power
definition: FoundationalAt F w essenceOf esseOf Received ComposedOfMatterAndForm CanFailToBe PowerOver f: f exists at w (the frame's world-relative existence); its represented esse equals its represented essence; it is not composed of matter and form; its esse is received in no principle (DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN); it is first in SIMPLY_PRIOR_1 (IsFirstBeing: whatever is simply prior to it is itself); nothing, itself included, is a CAUSE_2 of its esse; it is incorruptible simply (no in-subject potency to non-being, POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_1, DEF-INCORRUPTIBLE-SIMPLY); and no being, itself included, has POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 over it. A defined conjunction over those parameters; its component terms keep their existing definitions and senses: can fail to be (DEF-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE, POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_1 of d25cee67-1d5c-4a4c-bda5-8571b731ddf3), POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 (3fd6bddb-f10c-4df4-8694-3eb5e7c28617, POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_2), CAUSE_2 (DEF-CAUSE-OF-PERFECTION), SIMPLY_PRIOR_1 (DEF-SIMPLE-PRIORITY), received esse (DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN). Every conjunct is non-modal: it says nothing about f's existence at any other world.
note: Stipulated for #1887 (docs/notes/modal-grounding-frameworks.md) as the matching scope at which the C2 crux is contested: the profile the C2 note's rivals and the First Way's mover share. Examples: on classical theism, God; on the brute-first rival, a contingent simple first actuality (the C2 note's bruteSimple). Non-examples: a creature (received esse, a cause of its esse, under the creator's power); a corruptible composite. Which conjuncts each account of possibility uses differs: PGP uses only actuality, incorruptibility and the no-power clause; the esse-identity route (B6) only actuality and esse = essence; the existence-conditional verdict uses none of the conjuncts beyond actuality (its essence clauses are separate premises); the combinatorial verdict uses none. Under the C2 batch's correlation premise the no-power clause follows from the uncaused and incorruptible clauses (controls, law 1), so it is not an extra stipulation there. Open obligations: whether the conjuncts are jointly satisfiable by a real being is not asserted. What would source it: a text characterizing the first cause by exactly these features (ST I q.3 a.4, q.3 a.7, De ente c.4; navigation only).
